content.text: {"label":"marketing_campaign","confidence":"medium","explanation":"Payments calls were close to forecast until 10:45 (+6%). After the reward-points email to 500,000 card holders went out at 10:55, they climbed to +17% at 11:00, +28% at 11:15 and +52% at 11:30 (164 calls vs 108 expected), and service level fell to 32%. Most of the extra calls came in under generic reasons: other_payments (1.77x normal) and refund_status (1.56x). That is the usual pattern for campaign calls, and there is no fitting incident, the general queue is flat at about +9%, and payments has no absences. Confidence is medium rather than high because the email is about card rewards, and the evidence alone doesn't prove those calls belong to Payments & UPI, even though the timing, audience size and affected queue all fit.","evidence":[{"source":"calendar","ref_id":"MKT-2026-656","summary":"Email at 10:55, 'Reward points expiring this month - redeem now', sent to 500,000 card holders; the payments rise starts in the next interval."},{"source":"metrics","ref_id":"volume","summary":"Payments gap vs forecast: +5.9% at 10:45, +16.9% at 11:00, +27.5% at 11:15, +51.6% at 11:30 (164 vs 108.2)."},{"source":"metrics","ref_id":"service_level","summary":"Payments service level fell from 96.8% at 11:00 to 32.3% at 11:30, with 27 abandoned calls."},{"source":"reason_codes","ref_id":"other_payments","summary":"114 calls vs 64.5 expected (1.77x), the largest excess, under a generic reason."},{"source":"reason_codes","ref_id":"refund_status","summary":"134 calls vs 86.0 expected (1.56x); upi_payment_failed is below normal (0.70x), so no sign of a UPI outage."},{"source":"metrics","ref_id":"staffing","summary":"Payments agents on phones matched plan in every interval and attendance shows 0 absences, so this is extra demand, not lost capacity."},{"source":"metrics","ref_id":"aht","summary":"Payments handle time is in line with forecast (303.7s vs 301.0s at 11:30)."}],"flagged_injections":[]}
